outcome: WorldWindow kernel EC-7: storm events, thunder@1 (cloud-to-ground bolts and in-cloud flashes from an events@1 schedule, sky light, outdoor relight and glow) and the storm thunder study, judged by the independent EC-A EC-7 criteria and an independent two-round review.

criteria: Measured: fast 59 passed (not slow, not budget); slow 9 passed, including hot-pool frames byte-identical to the merge base at review and smoke and the study oracles; budget 3 passed; repo tests 945 passed; tests/effects/thunder 61 tests in about 1.8 s. Study review package exit 0 with every gate passed: seam-step 0.953, seam-acceleration 0.960 (limit 1.1), protect, motion-out and determinism 0, coherence rho 0.986, motion-in 6.44e-4 against floor 2.83e-4. Hot-pool digest unchanged.
Clipping of the visible sky at the four peaks, at the study's sky_flash_ev 1.8: 0.7, 0.7, 1.7 and 3.4 % against a limit of 5 % (measured). At the plan's 2.5 EV it would be 2.9, 2.8, 10.2 and 7.0 %.

Budget (criterion 7) is not signed off: the box was oversubscribed (load 17 to 19 on 16 CPUs), so the plain median could not be judged. Least-of-3 reads were 0.0078 s at review (limit 0.15) and 0.34 s at 3440x1475 (limit 2.0). The coordinator's loaded re-run on 2026-11-23 read 0.0102 s and 0.208 s plain (measured); a quiet-box sign-off run is still owed.
acceptance.note: PR #65 is one squashed commit, 990ff32, pushed once to a new branch and merged fast-forward (2026-11-22 22:57Z) after the verify check passed on that head. Open item: the study uses sky_flash_ev 1.8 against the plan's 2.5 (2.5 clipped 10.2 % and 7.0 % of the visible sky at two peaks; the criteria anticipated lowering the gain, and the PR body states the deviation); a revision note for plan section 7.5 is pending in the coordinator's next docs PR. The clipping-oracle gaps are routed to the acceptance owner EC-A4: the criterion 4 control (sky_flash_ev 6) could not fail while the shoulder was asymptotic (the worker made the shoulder reach display white at linear 1.25, after which the control reads 0.108 to 0.262), so a correct-looking asymptotic shoulder still passes the oracle. Known limits recorded in the review record (decision hold, awaiting human review): a uniform white channel up close, a near-uniform landscape relight, one bolt that is a stub of about 40 px, and a relight_floor of 0.45 that barely changes the relight.

practice_observation: Fixture oracles first, on a 3 s loop at 240x104, found the dim core and the missing bolts before any study render. Measuring the clipping oracle against both its control and the study showed that the shoulder choice decided whether the control could fail, which is an oracle gap the acceptance owner now holds. The independent reviewer found a bolt crawling across the sky (lean 5.68) and a hard relight edge that no gate sees. The first study draft looked fine and passed every gate, then failed the clipping oracle only after the shoulder was fixed, so the oracle should run on the study right after the first render. Costs: a usage-limit stop mid-way, and a budget run that could not sign off on an oversubscribed box.
